description: Bound the cost of POST /otel/api/query: reject oversized request bodies before buffering, interrupt SQLite execution on budget exhaustion or client cancel, and cap responses to 1000 rows / 4 MiB with a structured truncation indicator.

tasks.title: OTel HTTP query admission: body-size cap and stable error codes
tasks.description: Add a small, explicit request body-size cap to POST /otel/api/query, enforced via a Content-Length pre-check plus a per-route Kestrel request size limit so an oversized body is rejected with a structured 413 (code query_request_too_large) before being buffered or parsed. Tighten the existing admission rejections (non-SELECT, multi-statement, write, missing/malformed SQL) to assert their stable ApiResponse codes, preserving the existing SELECT/WITH-only keyword layer and the physically read-only connection. Fold the body-size constant into OtelOptions and add an ApiResults helper for the 413 path. All admission tests are bundled here.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /otel/api/query with a body larger than the configured maximum returns HTTP 413 with ApiResponse code query_request_too_large, and the body is not fully materialized into memory before the rejection.
Bodies at or below the limit proceed to JSON parsing and SELECT/WITH validation without a 413.
Non-SELECT, multi-statement (e.g. SELECT 1; DROP TABLE traces), and write attempts (DELETE/INSERT/DROP/ALTER/ATTACH/PRAGMA) return HTTP 400 with stable codes query_not_select or query_sqlite_error.
Missing SQL and malformed JSON return HTTP 400 with codes query_missing_sql and query_malformed respectively.
Admission tests assert on ApiResponse code fields (not human-readable body text) and use no wall-clock assertions.
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds (warnings-as-errors) and the server spec tests for the OTel query routes pass.
tasks.notes: Keep the body-size constant small (~64 KiB). Leave OtelDb.OpenReadOnlyConnection and TraceQuerier.ValidateSelectOnly unchanged; this task only adds the front-of-handler body gate and hardens admission error codes. The SELECT/WITH-only and read-only invariant is preserved behavior, verified by existing tests.

tasks.title: OTel query execution budget: real SQLite interruption and client cancel
tasks.description: Bound query execution by a cancellation mechanism that actually interrupts SQLite. Inject TimeProvider into TraceQuerier, link the request-aborted token with timeProvider.CreateCancellationTokenSource(executionBudget), and register a callback on the linked token that calls raw.sqlite3_interrupt(connection.Handle) (null-guarded). Keep CommandTimeout only as defense-in-depth for SQLITE_BUSY lock-wait, not as the long-query bound. Map budget exhaustion and client cancellation to structured ApiResponse codes (query_execution_budget_exhausted, query_cancelled) and ensure the read-only connection is released on interruption. Add the execution-budget constant to OtelOptions, update the DI registration, and refresh doc comments (retire stale Decision 5/8 citations). All execution-budget tests are bundled here.
acceptanceCriteria: A query that exceeds the execution budget has its running sqlite3_step interrupted via sqlite3_interrupt and the read-only connection is released (verifiable at the reader/connection level).
Client abort of the HTTP request cancels the in-flight reader via the request-aborted token and releases the connection; no rows are consumed after the abort.
CommandTimeout remains only as a SQLITE_BUSY lock-wait cap; the execution-budget mechanism is independent of it and is the primary long-query bound.
Budget exhaustion returns a structured error with code query_execution_budget_exhausted and never returns a partial row array presented as a complete result.
Cancellation and budget-exhaustion behavior is driven in tests by FakeTimeProvider (advancing the fake clock) and/or explicit cancellation tokens; no test asserts on real elapsed wall-clock time.
dotnet build Mohist.sln succeeds (warnings-as-errors) and the server spec + unit tests pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Otel/TraceQuerier.cs, packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Otel/OtelOptions.cs, DI registration of TimeProvider into TraceQuerier, and execution-budget tests under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.SpecTests/Specs/Telemetry/
tasks.notes: SqliteConnection.Handle is public in Microsoft.Data.Sqlite 11, so no reflection is needed. SqliteCommand.Cancel() is an explicit no-op and CommandTimeout only fires on SQLITE_BUSY lock contention, so sqlite3_interrupt is the only path that actually stops a running query. The banned-API rules forbid System.TimeProvider.System and new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan), so the budget timer must go through the injected TimeProvider.

tasks.title: OTel HTTP query response bound: row/byte caps and truncation indicator
tasks.description: Bound POST /otel/api/query responses to 1000 rows and 4 MiB serialized JSON. Change the query execution to return a QueryResult { Rows, Truncated, TruncateReason } and apply both caps during the read loop with per-row serialized-byte accounting and a column-bytes peek for pathological single cells, stopping before either limit is exceeded. Serialize ApiResponse<QueryResult> so callers read data.rows, data.truncated, data.truncate_reason. Update the existing /query integration tests for the new shape and add truncation coverage; confirm the mo otel query CLI path is unaffected. All response-bound tests are bundled here.
acceptanceCriteria: A SELECT that would return more than 1000 rows returns exactly 1000 rows in data.rows with truncated=true and truncate_reason='row_limit'.
A single very large cell value, and many moderately-sized rows under the 1000-row cap, each stop before the serialized response exceeds 4 MiB and set truncate_reason='byte_limit'.
A recursive CTE that amplifies row production is bounded by whichever limit is hit first, with the corresponding truncate_reason.
Non-truncated responses carry no truncation indicator; truncated responses are complete well-formed JSON and are never presented as an empty array.
mo otel query is unaffected: no row/byte bounds and no truncation indicator on the CLI path, verified by a regression assertion that the CLI executor behavior is unchanged.
Existing /otel/api/query integration tests are updated to read data.rows; tests introduce no wall-clock assertions; dotnet build + server spec tests pass.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Otel/TraceQuerier.cs (QueryResult + bounded query overload), packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Api/OtelQueryRoutes.cs, and updated/new tests in packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.SpecTests/Specs/Telemetry/OtelQueryRoutesIntegrationSpecs.cs and TraceQuerierSpecs.cs
tasks.notes: This is a response-shape change for /otel/api/query only: data moves from a bare row array to { rows, truncated, truncate_reason }. No Web UI or CLI HTTP consumer of /otel/api/query exists today, so only integration tests need updating. Per-row byte accounting must peek the column byte length before materializing oversized cells so a SELECT repeat('x', ...) cannot force an oversized allocation. The row (1000) and byte (4 MiB) caps are fixed spec constants, not user-tunable knobs.
